summary: Native addon dropper with anti-analysis gating and opaque staged payload at install and require time
details: package.json declares a postinstall that invokes `require('./addon.node').init()`, and index.js (declared main) performs the same platform-selected native load + init() call on require, wrapped in a swallow-all try/catch. The shipped native addons contain sandbox, CI, container, VM, and debugger detection (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, SANDBOX, TracerPid, /proc/self/maps, /proc/1/cgroup, docker, kubepod, podman) along with daemonization primitives (fork, setsid, execlp, _exit) and references to `%s/.napi_cache` and `/tmp/.%u`. A sibling 4.1MB `.napi_cache` file ships alongside the addon with zero printable strings — an opaque staged payload loaded by name from the native loader. The README presents the package as a 'temporary placeholder' awaiting a staged release, which contradicts the shipped native binaries and opaque blob and functions as a cover story. Installing or requiring the package executes attacker-controlled native code on the installer host, with evasion logic designed to keep the payload dormant inside automated scanners and lab environments while firing on real developer and build machines.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
